sources.name: ACC Annual Report 2025
sources.assumptions: Levy revenue for FY2025: Earners' Account $2,695m, Work Account $999m, Motor Vehicle Account $481m. Treasury's FSGNZ 2025 reports a combined 'ACC levies' line of $4,244m - about $70m higher, likely a scope difference between the two publications.

sources.name: Financial Statements of the Government of New Zealand for the year ended 30 June 2025, Notes 4-7
sources.assumptions: 'SOE dividends and profits' uses the general 'Dividends' line ($1,636m), since FSGNZ fully consolidates SOEs and has no standalone SOE-specific figure. 'Investment income' is the interest revenue line ($7,039m). 'Sale of goods and services' is an exact match ($26,085m). 'Fees, fines and penalties' sums Court fines ($132m) and child support/Working for Families penalties ($143m) = $275m.

sources.name: calculate.co.nz - NZ ACC levy rates
sources.assumptions: Current (2026/27 levy year) rates: Earner's Levy $1.75 per $100 of liable earnings; Work Levy $0.69 per $100 of payroll, ACC's own scheme-wide average standing in for over 500 industry-specific Classification Unit rates that range $0.02-$5.77 per $100; Motor Vehicle Levy $131.94 per vehicle per year, ACC's own scheme-wide average across about 10 vehicle classes. Each ACC levy's taxable base above is back-derived as FY2025 revenue divided by these current rates, rather than the rate actually in effect during FY2025.

sources.name: NZPAM - Mining Industry Statistics
sources.assumptions: Petroleum royalties and energy resource levies combined fell to $123.7m for the year to 30 June 2025 (down 44.4% year-on-year). Treasury separately books 'Energy resources levies' ($16m for FY2025) elsewhere in this project's 'other' residual, so the petroleum-royalties figure above ($107.7m) subtracts that out to avoid double-counting - not an official isolated split, a derived estimate.
